title: What if I need legal representation to help with my tax problem but can’t afford it? | Internal Revenue Service
text: Skip to main content What if I need legal representation to help with my tax problem but can’t afford it? More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Multimedia center Tax articles to share Posters to share Low Income Taxpayer Clinics (LITCs) assist low income taxpayers before the Internal Revenue Service, assist taxpayers in audits, appeals and collection disputes, and can help taxpayers respond to IRS notices and to correct account problems. If you are a low income taxpayer who cannot afford professional tax assistance or if you speak English as a second language (ESL) and need help understanding your taxpayer rights and responsibilities, you may qualify for help from an LITC that provides assistance for free or for a nominal charge. Although LITCs receive partial funding from the IRS, LITCs, their employees, and their volunteers are completely independent of, and are not associated with, the federal government. The LITCs are generally operated by nonprofit organizations or academic institutions. Each LITC independently decides if you meet the income guidelines and other criteria before it agrees to represent you.. You can find an LITC located in or near your area by using Publication 4134, Low Income Taxpayer Clinic List PDF . This publication identifies all LITCs who represent low income taxpayers before the IRS or provide ESL services, and is available at IRS.gov/advocate or your local IRS office. Low income taxpayers also may be able to receive assistance from a referral system operated by state bar associations, state or local societies of accountants, and other nonprofit tax professional organizations.
